So, in order to COLLECT information of intelligence value from someone, in order to spy on them, you FIRST have to establish what's called a criminal predicate.

"Criminal predicate" is an extremely important legal term. Before you can collect information of intelligence value against a target, you HAVE to have a REASON to believe that criminal activity has taken place or is imminent. You have to be able to prove in court that your collection was justified. You have to be able to SHOW how you had legitimately come to conclude that there's criminal activity taking place. The evidence that criminal activity is taking place is called the criminal predicate.

This criminal predicate can take many forms. It doesn't have to be undeniable proof of criminal activity, but a reasonable justification. Suppose someone tips you off, like someone calling the police and saying that they think their neighbor is selling drugs out of their house. This alone doesn't establish a criminal predicate, but it enables police to look into it. If they see that this is in fact taking place, now they have a criminal predicate, and they can tap their phones, set up surveillance, etc. Now they can collect information to be used later in court to make their case against them.
